newsitem.title: USA: Odwalla says product recall cut sales.
newsitem.headline: Odwalla says product recall cut sales.

text.p: Odwalla Inc said a 14 percent increase in first quarter sales to $14.1 million was offset by the costs incurred in connection with its product recall on October 30, 1996, resulting in a net loss of $4.8 million, or $0.98 per share for the first quarter.

Odwalla said it experienced a significant reduction in sales of all products after the October 30 voluntary recall of products containing apple juice and, on October 31, 1996, the expanded recall of its carrot and vegetable products.
Odwalla also incurred significant costs for the product recalled and destroyed, legal and marketing expenses.

Additional costs were incurred with the introduction of the flash pasteurization process, it said. Direct recall costs totaled $3.8 million in the first quarter, including $700,000 of estimated direct costs for the rest of the year.
Gross margin rose to 50 percent of net sales versus 45 percent in the year-ago period.
Operating expenses were $12.9 million versus $5.9 million a year ago.

Odwalla said it will continue to invest and expand. As a result of the plans for continued growth and infrastructure development, it has not reduced costs commensurate with the reduction of sales following the recall, it said. Its cash position was $9.0 million as of November 30, 1996.
